title: Story structure: three acts
examples: Where does the story really start to get exciting?
What is the most important part of the story?
How do filmmakers build tension in a movie?

explain.say: The first part of a story is the set up. This part introduces the characters and the world.
Next, the story moves to confrontation. This is where the main problem gets bigger.
The turning point is a major moment. It changes the direction of the story suddenly.
The final act is the resolution. Here, the main conflict is finally sorted out.
In real life, think about learning to ride a bike. The set up is learning the basics.
A common mistake is thinking the set up and confrontation are the same. They are not.

faq.q: What is the difference between the climax and the resolution?
faq.a: The climax is the most exciting peak of action. The resolution is what happens right after the peak, where things calm down.
asks: Does the ending happen right after the peak?

faq.q: Does every story have these three acts?
faq.a: Most traditional stories follow this three-act structure. However, some modern films play with these rules.
asks: Can a story skip these parts?

faq.q: What is the purpose of the set up?
faq.a: The set up's job is to make you care about the characters. It shows what life is like before the trouble starts.
asks: Why do we need the beginning?
What does the set up teach us?

faq.q: How is a turning point different from the climax?
faq.a: The turning point is a single event that changes everything. The climax is the peak action that results from that change.
asks: Is the turning point the same as the big fight?
What makes a moment a turning point?

faq.q: If a story has no conflict, does it still have a structure?
faq.a: Yes, even calm stories have structure. The set up still shows the normal life, and the resolution shows the final state.
asks: Can a peaceful story be structured?
What if there is no villain?

facts: The three-act structure is a common model for narrative storytelling.
The set up establishes the 'normal world' before the conflict begins.
The confrontation section builds tension towards the highest point of action.
The resolution shows the aftermath and the new normal for the characters.

quiz.say: A story begins by showing a character's ordinary routine. This is the:
quiz.why: The set up is where you meet the characters and see their normal life.

wrong.0: The resolution happens at the very end, after everything is solved.
wrong.1: A turning point is a specific moment, not the whole beginning section.
wrong.3: This is too late; confrontation happens when the problem starts.

quiz.say: The main problem escalates, and the character faces increasing obstacles. This is the:
quiz.why: Confrontation is the middle act where the tension builds up with rising action.

wrong.0: The resolution means the problem is already solved by this point.
wrong.1: This describes the whole middle section, not just one key moment.
wrong.3: The set up is calm and shows life before the problem.

quiz.say: A character discovers a secret map that changes their entire journey. This moment is best described as a:
quiz.why: A turning point is a single, significant event that forces the story forward.

wrong.0: This is too big an event to just be part of the beginning.
wrong.1: The climax is the peak of action, not necessarily the moment of discovery.
wrong.2: The resolution happens after the big changes have already occurred.
